reviewer: Primary Codex agent; source/image inspection, not a human review
observations: All six current native/source views inspected. Full original HB71,HB111 and SNL21 preserve assembly context; comparison panels have independent scales.
The outer drum follows the lining face and turns into the mounting flange. The toothed flywheel closes the engine end and keeps its tapered/keyed bore open for the future crankshaft.

The saved flywheel has a steeper hub-to-rim flare in axial section than the handbook sketch. Its provisional dish fits the inherited bearing, cone and plunger interfaces; the complete engine/crankshaft installation must revisit this profile. No calibrated dimensional agreement is claimed.
The SNL dashed flywheel envelope is proportionally larger than the selected HB19.811in diameter. This remains a recorded source conflict.

The exposed-wire view shows two separate circular routes through six heads each, with their paired tails turning inward between neighboring heads. The old axial plunger-wire tail would intersect the dish.
The rear flywheel view exposes the long positive-drive hub and through keyway. Hub spline ownership remains an interpretation in conflict with the handbook wording about crankshaft teeth.
The tooth detail shows the selected involute form and continuous rim. Actual historical tooth count, pressure angle and starter engagement are unresolved.
The shaft and its nut/key retention are visibly absent. The finished engine and complete clutch are not claimed.
